Welcome to

Under the oak

Blue Bayou sits on Canal Street at the edge of the French Quarter, with the streetcar stopping right outside. Inside, a thirty-foot oak hung with Spanish moss and lanterns spreads over the dining room, the oyster bar glows blue along one wall, and there's a band on stage every night until close.

1 / 3The dining room, under the oak

From the oyster bar

Shucked to order, fired over open flame

Louisiana oysters, opened when you order them. Take a stool at the bar and watch the shuckers work and the butter hit the coals. Chargrilled, Rockefeller and Creole come six to an order.

  • Famous ChargrilledCajun garlic and herb butter, parmesan and Romano
  • Raw on the Half ShellIce cold, with all the fixings half dozen $15, dozen $27
  • RockefellerSpinach, rich cream and cheese
  • CreoleCreole tomato and garlic sauce
#1

Voted best oystersby the readers of Where Y'at Magazine

Eating raw or undercooked shellfish carries risk. If you have chronic illness of the liver, stomach or blood, or an immune disorder, order your oysters fully cooked.
